chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Fadhl from Dawud ibn Farqad said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who was traveling with him, and with him was a female slave and two male slaves. He said to them, 'You are free for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, and testify that what is in the belly of this female slave of mine is from me.' She gave birth to a boy. When they arrived, the heirs denied this and re-enslaved them. Then the two boys were freed after that, and they testified after their freedom that their first master had testified to them that what was in the belly of his female slave was from him. He (peace be upon him) said, 'Their testimony is valid for the boy, and the boy who testified for him will not re-enslave them, because they have established his lineage.'

key_terms.لِوَجْهِ اَللَّهِ: For the sake of God (a phrase indicating manumission)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal effect of a master freeing his slaves and testifying to the paternity of a child in his slave woman's womb?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the interplay between manumission (*itq*) and paternity declaration (*iqrar*) in the context of a slave woman's pregnancy. The ruling establishes that the freed slaves' testimony validates the boy's lineage, preventing the heirs from re-enslaving him, as their emancipation and testimony serve as mutual confirmation of his free status and descent from the master.
